text:
mike: Heads-up — noticed a ~1.7x token latency regression on PP runs after yesterday's kernel-selector tweak. Profiling attached below.

keiko: Can you paste the short flame/prof? Which kernel got picked by the selector?

mike: Quick snip from the runtime trace: 
```
selector: matmul_kernel=auto -> chosen=cuBLASLt_fallback
model: redwood-7b, pp=2,tp=2, microbatch=8, 1F1B
avg token latency: 85ms -> 145ms
p99 token latency: 320ms -> 560ms
all-reduce step time: +35% (measured across stages)
KV cache hitrate (warmup): 0.98 -> 0.82
memcpy spikes at stage boundary: +28ms per step
```

anya: oof. cuBLASLt_fallback for those leading dims is a known pathological case. Did the selector prefer a quantized kernel path or disable split-k?

samir: adding to that — metrics show KV evictions increased during warmup. Might be an interaction: microbatching pattern + cache evictions -> more recompute traffic crossing pipeline boundary.

mike: repro command I used: `./tools/run_pp_profile --model redwood-7b --pp 2 --tp 2 --microbatch 8 --steps 200 --profile out.json`

keiko: ran the same locally, captured per-phase breakdown: 
```
[profile sample]
step 45: stage0 compute=42ms, stage0 memcpy=30ms, stage1 compute=40ms, all-reduce=28ms, idle=45ms
loss of overlap observed at microbatch boundary between stage0->stage1
```
Looks like memcpy+all-reduce is pushing past compute window so 1F1B can't hide comm.

jordan: Could this be because the kernel selector now biases toward shape-stable kernels and disables split-k or split-accum heuristics for matmul? That would increase peak memcpy when shapes are not divisible.

anya: try forcing `--kernel-prefer=splitk` or `--kernel-prefer=legacy` to see impact. Also check NCCL algorithm: ring vs tree fallback showed up in logs last night. Ring is usually better for our shape sizes.

mike: quick experiment results: forced `--kernel-prefer=splitk` -> avg token latency down to ~96ms, all-reduce time reduced ~12%, memcpy spikes gone. KV hitrate returned to ~0.97.

samir: nice. Action items: (1) add microbatch-aware penalty to kernel selector so it won't pick fallback kernels that increase stage memcpy; (2) add profiler alert when memcpy_at_boundary > threshold; (3) tune KV eviction window to account for microbatch cadence. I'll draft RFC.

infra-bot: deploy 2026-03-18T09:20:00 by mike: rolling back kernel-selector tweak in canary -> off :white_check_mark:

mike: After rollback, canary runs look back to baseline. But we still need selector guardrails and a regression test in perf CI that exercises PP+1F1B at varied microbatch sizes.

keiko: I'll add a small harness that sweeps microbatch {4,8,16} and auto-checks overlap ratio and memcpy spikes, then fail the perf gate if overlap drops >20%.

jordan: And add a quick check in model onboarding: if chosen kernel increases memcpy at stage boundary by >20% vs baseline, mark as "requires manual review" and don't auto-promote.

anya: Great. Also log for posterity — observed root cause: selector fallback to cuBLASLt_fallback + NCCL algorithm fallback created a compound regression when microbatch boundary memcopies couldn't overlap with compute.

mike: TL;DR: regression introduced by kernel-selector tweak; mitigated by rollback; long-term fix = microbatch-aware selector heuristic + perf CI guardrail + KV eviction tuning. I'll open the follow-ups. :memo:

samir: I'll own the RFC and the perf test. Keiko, ping me when the harness PR is ready and I'll add the CI job.

mike: thanks everyone, great triage.
